provider: Global Dam Watch / Figshare archival record
api_version: Figshare API v2; frozen public article 25988293, version 1

request_contract.parameter_rules: Exactly one explicit opt-in anonymous GET of https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/25988293/versions/1. No caller-selected ID, version, URL, query, headers, redirects, pagination, archive download, file URL follow, or second request. Public article metadata only. Any changed version, licence or file-list identity blocks. The first live receipt must be reviewed before scientific/data promotion.

response_contract.format: Figshare public, immutable-version-targeted article details JSON: article ID 25988293, version 1, exact version DOI and CC BY 4.0; metadata describing two alternate v1.0 ZIP representations (gdb and shp) only. Reject unverified/missing required metadata instead of assuming files.
response_contract.scientific_semantics: Global Dam Watch v1.0 is a global river-barrier and reservoir reference database. The published release contains a barrier point layer and an associated reservoir polygon layer; these are distinct scientific objects linked by identifiers/location, and not every barrier has an associated reservoir polygon. The two release ZIPs are alternate Geodatabase and Shapefile delivery representations, not independent scientific releases. The published v1.0 inventory reports 41,145 barrier points and 35,295 associated reservoir polygons. Presence in the database does not establish dam-failure probability, structural fragility, reservoir operating state, current asset status, downstream inundation or catastrophe-model fitness.

operational_constraints.rate_limit_notes: Figshare official API documentation recommends at most one request per second and reserves throttle/block rights. This contract permits one explicitly invoked fixed metadata GET without pagination, redirects, retry, file retrieval or a scheduled acquisition loop.
operational_constraints.mutability_notes: Use the version-specific /versions/1 API route rather than mutable latest article details. Archive file identities, declared sizes and optional provider MD5 from that response are metadata, not verified original ZIP bytes. A live result must record retrieval UTC, response byte count/SHA-256 and code identity. For archived file acquisition, separately review exact asset, permissions, declared and independently computed SHA-256 and CRS/column semantics.

rights_and_policy.notes: The exact Global Dam Watch v1.0 Figshare dataset record states CC BY 4.0, and the peer-reviewed data paper likewise identifies GDW v1.0 as available under CC BY 4.0. Figshare's public Data Access Policy and API guidance allow public metadata/data access and API mining subject to the content licence. These verified rights and service permissions are ceilings, not repository execution or publication approval: this contract deliberately remains documented_only with no live probe or file request. Any persisted sample still requires exact asset identity, provenance, required attribution and repository review before bytes are committed or published.

expected_evidence: exact version-specific Figshare metadata endpoint HTTP 200 without redirect
strict bounded UTF-8 application/json; response byte count and SHA-256
CC BY 4.0 licence identity from provider metadata
exact two alternate archive names, item identifiers, positive declared sizes and any provider MD5
retrieval UTC and execution code identity
no archive download, provider bytes persisted, CAT admission or database write

notes: A single fixed, version-specific Figshare public metadata canary is ready for explicitly opted-in execution, never an unbounded harvester. It cannot retrieve either archive, follow links or admit GIS source data. Publisher paper confirms 41,145 barriers and 35,295 reservoir polygons; 5,850 barrier points have no matched polygon. The source is not dam-failure hazard or insured loss. First live provider response remains unverified in this change.
